analysis_summary.notes: This patch adds only kernel BPF selftest code under tools/testing/selftests/bpf/. All 5 hunks are exclusively in test files: 4 hunks in prog_tests/kprobe_multi_test.c (test runner) and 1 hunk creating a new test BPF program kprobe_multi_sleepable.c. No kernel source, UAPI header, syscall, ioctl, netlink, proc/sys/sysfs, CLI, or configuration code is changed. The patch adds a new test case (fail_9) that validates the kernel's behavior of rejecting sleepable kprobe_multi programs, along with the required test BPF program. All candidates were evaluated and determined to be internal test-only additions with no external observable compatibility impact.

candidate_dispositions.reason: Adds a new #include for test skeleton header kprobe_multi_sleepable.skel.h. Purely a test infrastructure header inclusion with no external impact.

Adds local variables LIBBPF_OPTS(bpf_test_run_opts, topts) and struct kprobe_multi_sleepable *sl_skel in test function test_attach_api_fails(). Used only within the test to run and destroy the sleepable kprobe_multi test program. No external impact.
Adds 'int saved_error, err;' local variable declarations in test function test_attach_api_fails(). Used to capture errno before ASSERT macros clobber it. No external impact.

Adds fail_9 test case block in test_attach_api_fails(). This test loads a kprobe_multi BPF program with BPF_F_SLEEPABLE flag, attempts to attach it, and asserts that the kernel correctly rejects the attachment with -EINVAL. It also runs the fentry program via bpf_prog_test_run_opts to verify the program loaded correctly. Purely a test addition verifying existing kernel behavior; does not change any kernel API or ABI.

New BPF test program file for the selftest. Contains a kprobe.multi SEC program that calls bpf_copy_from_user (a sleepable-only helper) and a fentry/bpf_fentry_test1 SEC program. This is a test artifact that would only be loaded by the selftest runner; it has no effect on the running kernel's behavior, API, ABI, or user-facing interfaces.
